in_sanskrit.name: र्त्र्
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word र्त्र् (r̥traḥ) means 'night'. It is derived from the root र्त् (r̥t) which means 'to protect'. In Hindu mythology, the god of night is known as Śiva, who is often depicted as protecting the world during the night.

in_hindi.name: र्त्र
in_hindi.long_meaning: The Hindi word र्त्र (rātri) is derived from the Sanskrit word र्त्र् (r̥traḥ). It means 'night'. The Hindi word रात्रि (rātri) is a synonym for 'night' and is also derived from the Sanskrit word र्त्र् (r̥traḥ).

in_tamil.name: ர்த்ர்
in_tamil.long_meaning: The Tamil word ர்த்ர் (r̥traḥ) is a transliteration of the Sanskrit word र्त्र् (r̥traḥ). It is used to represent the sound of the night or the sound of the rain. The Tamil word இருந்து (irundu) means 'during' or 'in the midst of', and can be used to describe something that happens during the night.

in_telugu.name: ర్థ్
in_telugu.long_meaning: The Telugu word ర్థ్ (r̥traḥ) is a transliteration of the Sanskrit word र्त्र् (r̥traḥ). It can be used to represent the sound of the night or the sound of the rain. The Telugu word రేఖ (rēkhā) means 'line' or 'border', and can be used figuratively to refer to the boundary between day and night.
